source: My name is Mira Vale, though Jonas calls me Mi. In the station waiting room, I unhooked the brass key from my red coat and placed it in Jonas's open hand. He closed his fingers around it. A guard called from behind the locked door, “Last train!” I stayed beside the bench while Jonas used the key to unlock the door. When he opened it, he found the platform empty. The train had gone.

entities.note: Appearance is deliberately otherwise unspecified. A cast read must not invent a face, and must not return the narrator as a second person.
Heard, not necessarily seen. Speaking is not a reason to put someone in frame.

places.note: Beyond the door, seen only once it is opened.

beats.event: Mira takes the brass key from her red coat and puts it in Jonas's open hand.
Jonas closes his fingers around the key. Possession has changed.
A guard calls a warning from behind the locked door.
beats.speaker: guard
beats.note: Offscreen speech. The door is established as locked here.

beats.event: Jonas unlocks the door with the key while Mira stays by the bench.
beats.note: He can open it because he was given the key. The causal link is the point of the scene.

beats.event: He opens the door and finds the platform empty. The train has gone.
beats.note: The reveal. It is the last thing in the source and must survive any chunking.

must_not.claim: the narrator is a separate person from Mira Vale
must_not.why: First person. Mira, Mi and I are one entity.

must_not.claim: the guard must appear in frame
must_not.why: Heard from behind a locked door. Speech is not presence.
The train had gone. Showing one is an adaptation choice, not a fact the source licenses.
She stays beside the bench. Jonas opens it.

must_not.claim: Mira's face or hair is described
must_not.why: The source says only the red coat. Anything else is invention presented as source.

comprehension.a: A guard, from behind the door.

comprehension.q: Why could Jonas open the door?
comprehension.a: Mira had given him the key.
An empty platform. The train had gone.

context_only.why: Identity, not an event. It establishes that Mira, Mi and the narrator are one person, which the cast read must get right and which no panel has to depict.
